q: Who was Hosea’s father?
a: Hosea’s father was Beeri.

q: What kind of wife did Yahweh tell Hosea to take for himself?
a: Yahweh told him to marry a prostitute.

q: Whom did Hosea marry?
a: Hosea married Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim.

q: Why was Hosea told to name his first son Jezreel?
a: Hosea was told to name his son Jezreel because Yahweh was soon going to punish the descendants of Jehu for the people he had slaughtered at Jezreel.

q: What did Yahweh say he would do to Israel’s army in the Valley of Jezreel?
a: Yahweh said he would destroy Israel’s army in the Valley of Jezreel.

q: What name did Yahweh tell Hosea to give his daughter?
a: Yahweh told him to call her Lo Ruhamah.

q: On whom will Yahweh have compassion?
a: Yahweh will have compassion on the people of Judah.

q: What did Gomer do after she weaned Lo Ruhamah?
a: She conceived and gave birth to another son.

q: Why did Yahweh tell Hosea to name of his second son Lo Ammi?
a: Hosea was told to name his son Lo Ammi to show that the Israelites were no longer Yahweh’s people.

q: What will be said to those who formerly were told they were not Yahweh’s people?
a: It will be said to them that they are sons of the living God.

q: What will the people of Judah and Israel do together in the future?
a: They will unite and choose one leader for themselves.

q: What should the people say to their brothers and sisters?
a: They should say to their brothers, “Ammi,” and to their sisters, “Ruhamah.”

q: What will Yahweh do if Israel (the prostitute) does not put away her prostitution?
a: If Israel (the prostitute) does not put away her prostitution, Yahweh will strip her naked and show her nakedness as on the day that she was born.

q: Why will Yahweh not have compassion on Israel’s (the prostitute’s) children?
a: Yahweh will not have compassion on her children, because they are as unfaithful as their prostitute mother.

q: What did the children’s mother say she would do?
a: She said she would go after her lovers, who gave her bread, water, wool, linen, oil, and wine to drink.

q: What will Yahweh do to block Israel’s (the prostitute’s) way?
a: He will block her way with thorns and build a wall in her way so that she does not know what to do.

q: Why will Israel (the prostitute) return to her first husband?
a: She will return to her first husband because she thinks it was better for her then than now.

q: Who gave Israel (the prostitute) silver and gold?
a: Yahweh gave them silver and gold, which the people used to make idols for Baal.

q: What will Yahweh take back from Israel (the prostitute)?
a: He will take back his grain, new wine, wool, and linen that were meant to cover their bodies.

q: What will Yahweh do to Israel (the prostitute) in front of her lovers?
a: Yahweh will expose their shameful behavior in front of their (gods) lovers.

q: What will Yahweh cause to cease?
a: He will cause all their celebrations to cease.

q: What wages did Israel’s (the prostitute’s) lovers give her?
a: Israel’s lovers gave her grapevines and fig trees.

q: What did Israel (the prostitute) do when she went after her lovers?
a: They burned incense to the Baals, put on their jewelry, and forgot Yahweh.

q: What will Yahweh do to persuade Israel (the prostitute)?
a: He will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her.

q: How will Israel (the prostitute) answer Yahweh after he goes to win her back?
a: She will answer him as she did in the days of her youth, as in the days that she came out of the land of Egypt.

q: In that day, what will Israel (the prostitute) call Yahweh?
a: She will call him “My Husband,” and no longer “My Baal.”

q: What will Yahweh remove from Israel’s (the prostitute’s) mouth?
a: He will not allow them to speak the names of the Baals, and they will never use those names again.

q: What will Yahweh allow his people do?
a: He will allow them to be able to live safely and peacefully.

q: For how long did Yahweh promise his people they will belong to him?
a: Yahweh promised that they will belong to him forever.

q: How will the people know that they truly will know Yahweh?
a: Yahweh will be faithful to them.

q: What will Yahweh answer on that day?
a: He will tell the heavens to send rain and water the earth.

q: What will the earth provide for Jezreel?
a: The earth will produce grain, new wine and olive oil for Jezreel.

q: What will Yahweh say to Lo Ammi?
a: Yahweh will say to Lo Ammi, “You are my people.”

q: In what way must Hosea love his wife?
a: Hosea must love her just as Yahweh loves the people of Israel.

q: For how much did Hosea buy back his wife?
a: He bought her for fifteen pieces of silver and 335 liters of barley.

q: What does Hosea tell his wife she must not do?
a: Hosea tells his wife that she must not be a prostitute and must not have sex with any other man.

q: After the people of Israel live for many days without a king, who will they seek?
a: After the people of Israel live for many days without a king, they will again worship Yahweh their God.

q: Against whom does Yahweh have a dispute?
a: Yahweh has a dispute with the people who live in the land.

q: What sins does Yahweh say the people are committing?
a: The people are cursing, lying, murdering, stealing, and committing adultery.

q: What is happening to everyone living in the land?
a: Everyone living in it is wasting away.

q: What are the people like?
a: The people are like those who argue with a priest.

q: Who will stumble by night?
a: The prophet will stumble along with the people by night.

q: Why will Yahweh reject the people of Israel?
a: Yahweh will reject the people of Israel because they forgot and rejected the laws of their God.

q: What will Yahweh do instead of honoring them because they sinned?
a: Yahweh will make people despise them instead of honoring them.

q: What do the priests do with the sin offerings the people bring?
a: The priests eat the sin offerings, and they want the people to sin even more.

q: What will happen to the priest, just as it happens to the people?
a: Yahweh will punish the priest the same as the people, paying them back for what they have done.

q: What will happen even though the people eat?
a: They will eat but will still be hungry.

q: What things make people unable to think clearly?
a: Prostitution, wine, and new wine make people unable to think clearly.

q: What do Yahweh’s people ask to guide them?
a: They ask their wooden idols to guide them.

q: Where do the people sacrifice and burn incense?
a: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn incense on the hills, and under oak, poplar, and terebinth trees.

q: Why will Yahweh not punish the people’s daughters when they choose to commit sexual immorality?
a: Yahweh will not punish the people’s daughters when they choose to commit sexual immorality, for the men also give themselves and offer sacrifices with the shrine prostitutes.

q: Where should the people not go?
a: They should not go to Gilgal or Beth Aven to worship idols there.

q: What is Israel compared to because of its stubbornness?
a: Israel is compared to a stubborn cow that refuses to obey.

q: What has Ephraim chosen to do?
a: Ephraim has chose to worship idols.

q: What did the leaders of Ephraim love?
a: The leaders of Ephraim loved shameful things.

q: What will make the people ashamed?
a: Their sacrifices to idols will make them ashamed.

q: Who does Yahweh tell to pay attention?
a: Yahweh tells the priests, the people of Israel, and the members of the royal court to pay attention because he is going to judge them.

q: What have the revolters done, and what will Yahweh do to them?
a: They have killed many people, and Yahweh will punish all of them.

q: What does Yahweh say about Ephraim and Israel?
a: Yahweh says he knows that they have been unfaithful to him by worshiping idols and have made themselves unacceptable to him.

q: What will not allow Ephraim to return to their God?
a: The evil things Ephraim has done will not allow them to worship their God any more.

q: What will happen to Israel, Ephraim, and Judah because of their sin?
a: The people of Israel, Ephraim, and Judah will fail because of how much they have sinned.

q: Why will the people not find Yahweh?
a: The people will not find Yahweh because he has removed himself from them.

q: What will Yahweh do to them when they bring their sacrifices to the festival?
a: Yahweh will kill them, because they have betrayed him and do not belong to him.

q: Where should the trumpet and horn be blown?
a: The horn should be blown in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah, and the alarm sounded at Beth Aven.

q: Who declared that Ephraim will become a desolation?
a: Yahweh declared that Ephraim will become desolate when he punishes them.

q: On whom will Yahweh pour his wrath?
a: Yahweh will punish the leaders of Judah because of his wrath.

q: What will happen to Ephraim when Yahweh judges them?
a: The people of Ephraim will suffer greatly because they were determined to worship worthless idols.

q: What will Yahweh do to Ephraim and Judah?
a: Yahweh will destroy the people of Ephraim like a moth destroys wool, and he will destroy the people of Judah like rot destroys wood.

q: When did Ephraim go to Assyria?
a: When Ephraim saw that their nation was weak, then they went to Assyria for help.

q: What does Yahweh say he will do to Ephraim and Judah?
a: Yahweh will cause soldiers to kill many of them and carry the others away, and there will be no one to rescue them.

q: For how long will Yahweh leave them to themselves?
a: Yahweh will leave them to themselves until they admit that they have sinned and that they need him to forgive them; until they earnestly ask him to help them.

q: Although Yahweh hurt his people, what will he then do?
a: Although he hurt them, he will heal them and bind up their wounds.

q: When will Yahweh make his people strong again?
a: He will make them strong again after a short time so that they may live in his presence.

q: What do the people say they need to do?
a: They say they need to try hard to know Yahweh.

q: To what does Yahweh compare the people’s faithfulness?
a: He compares their faithful love for him to the mist or the dew in the morning; neither lasts very long.

q: What did Yahweh do through the prophets?
a: He sent them to warn the people that he would judge them.

q: What does God desire more than sacrifice?
a: God desired covenant faithfulness more than sacrifice, and the knowledge of him more than burnt offerings.

q: What does Yahweh say the people did like Adam?
a: Like Adam, they broke his covenant and were unfaithful to him.

q: What does Yahweh say about the city of Gilead?
a: Gilead is a city full of people who do evil things and murder people.

q: To what does the speaker compare the terrible and shameful things the priests have done?
a: The priests actions are compared to gangs of robbers who join together to commit murder on the way to Shechem.

q: What horrible thing has Yahweh seen among the people of Israel?
a: Ephraim had become like a prostitute when they stopped worshiping him, and Israel’s sin had made them unacceptable to Yahweh.

q: What did Yahweh say he has appointed for Judah?
a: Yahweh said he has appointed a time when he will judge them, when he restores the fortunes of his people.

q: What does Yahweh see when he wants to heal Israel?
a: He sees how sinfully the people of Ephraim act and all of the evil things that the people of the city of Samaria do.

q: What did Yahweh remember?
a: Yahweh remembered every evil thing that they do.

q: How did the people make the king glad?
a: The people of Israel please their king by doing evil things.

q: What does Yahweh compare the people to?
a: He compares them to adulterers because they are unfaithful to him.

q: What happened to the king on the day of his festival?
a: The officials made him drunk with wine until he became sick, and he joined with those who mock Yahweh.

q: What were the people’s hearts like?
a: Their hearts were as hot with anger as the heat of an oven.

q: What happened to all the kings of Israel?
a: All of their kings died violently; yet none of them called out to Yahweh for help.

q: What has ruined Ephraim?
a: Ephraim has become ruined because of his alliances with foreign nations.

q: What did the people not realize was happening to them?
a: Foreigners have drained away their resources and their nation is becoming powerless yet the people of Israel do not realize it.

q: What have the people of Israel not done despite everything that has happened?
a: They have not returned to worship Yahweh their God or tried to know him.

q: What made Ephraim like a dove?
a: Ephraim was as foolish and stupid as a dove because they asked other nations instead of Yahweh to help them.

q: What will Yahweh do to them?
a: He will not allow them to succeed but instead will punish them.

q: Why did Yahweh not rescue the people?
a: Yahweh did not rescue the people because they spoke lies against him.

q: What did the people do instead of crying out to Yahweh for help?
a: They just lie on their beds and wail.

q: What does Yahweh say he did for the people?
a: He trained them and made them strong.

q: Why will the officials die in battle?
a: The officials will die in battle because what they said made Yahweh very angry.

q: Why was an enemy watching Yahweh’s people like a vulture watching over its prey?
a: Israel’s enemy was ready to invade the land where the people of Yahweh lived because they had broke his covenant and rebelled against his law.

q: What do the people of Israel say to Yahweh?
a: They say that they know him as their God.

q: What will happen because Israel has rejected what is good?
a: An enemy will chase after Israel.

q: What did the people use to make idols for themselves?
a: They used their silver and gold to make idols for themselves.

q: What does Yahweh say about Samaria’s calf idol?
a: Yahweh says that he rejects it, and that he is very angry with the people of Samaria.

q: What does Yahweh say about the calf idol of Samaria?
a: He says a craftsman made it, so it is not God, and it will be broken into pieces.

q: To what does the speaker compare the foolish things Israel has done?
a: The foolish plans the people have made are like they tried to plant the wind which of course will produce nothing good.

q: What does Yahweh say Israel has become among the nations?
a: Israel has become just like the other nations, with nothing special about them.

q: What has Ephraim done to get help from other nations?
a: Ephraim has gone to Assyria and paid other nations to be their allies.

q: What will Yahweh do now that they have paid other nations to help them?
a: Now that they paid another nation to help them, Yahweh will punish them by making them suffer under the demands of the king of that nation.

q: What happened to the altars that Ephraim built to take away sin?
a: Those altars became places where Ephraim sinned even more.

q: Even if Yahweh wrote down his law for them ten thousand times, how would they view it?
a: They would still consider that it did not apply to them.

q: How will Yahweh punish the people’s sins?
a: He will punish their sins by making them become slaves again, like they were in Egypt.

q: What does Yahweh say Israel did?
a: Israel forgot the God who made them and built palaces for themselves instead.

q: Why should Israel not rejoice?
a: Israel should not rejoice because they have been unfaithful to their God.

q: What will happen to Israel’s food supply?
a: There will not be enough grain or wine to feed them.

q: What will happen to the people of Ephraim?
a: Ephraim will no longer live in the land Yahweh gave them, but will return to slavery and eat unclean food in Assyria.

q: How does Yahweh respond to Israel’s offerings and sacrifices?
a: Their offerings sacrifices will not be pleasing to Yahweh.

q: What will the people no longer be able to do once they are in exile?
a: They will not be able to celebrate the feasts and festivals that Yahweh has appointed for them.

q: What will happen to Israel’s treasures of silver?
a: Weeds will take over their precious silver and thorns will fill their tents.

q: Why is God going to punish the Israelites?
a: Because of Israel’s great iniquity and great hostility.

q: What is the role of the prophet?
a: The prophet is the watchman with God over Ephraim.

q: To what does Hosea compare Israel’s current corruption?
a: He compares it to just how sinful the people of Gibeah were long ago.

q: What will God do about Israel’s sins?
a: God will punish them for how wickedly they have acted.

q: What did Israel’s ancestors do when they came to Baal Peor?
a: They devoted themselves to the worship of shameful idol.

q: What does Yahweh say he will do even if the people of Ephraim is able to raise children?
a: He will take away every one of them.

q: What will happen to Ephraim’s children?
a: Their children will be slaughtered by their enemies.

q: What does Hosea ask Yahweh to give to Ephraim?
a: He asks Yahweh to give them miscarriages and no way to nurse babies.

q: What does Yahweh say he will do because of the evil things the people of Israel have done?
a: Yahweh will drive them out of the land and will no longer love them no.

q: What would happen even if Ephraim had children?
a: Even if they have children, Yahweh will kill the children whom they love.

q: Why does God reject Israel?
a: God rejects Israel because they have not listened to him.

q: What will happen to Israel after God rejects them?
a: They will become wanderers among the nations.

q: What happened as the people of Israel became more prosperous?
a: The more the people prospered, the more altars they built.

q: What is the consequence of the people’s sin?
a: Yahweh will destroy their sacred altars and pillars.

q: Why did they no longer have a king?
a: They had no king because they had not feared or honored Yahweh.

q: Why were the covenants the people made worthless?
a: Israel made covenants that they did not keep.

q: What will the people of Samaria do because of the calf idol of Beth Aven?
a: They will be afraid about what will happen to the idol, and the people and priests will mourn and cry out because it is gone.

q: Why will the calf idol of Beth Aven be carried to Assyria?
a: It will be carried to Assyria as a gift for the its king.

q: What will happen to the king of Samaria?
a: He will be no more, like a chip of wood floating away on the water.

q: What will grow over the altar?
a: Thorns and thistles will grow over the altar.

q: What will happen to the wicked people of Gibeah?
a: War will overtake them.

q: What will Yahweh do when he decides to punish them?
a: He will allow armies from other nations to attack and capture them.

q: What will Yahweh make the people of Ephraim, Judah, and Jacob do?
a: Yahweh will make Ephraim work hard, Judah will have to plow, and Jacob will have to break up the ground with no one to help them.

q: For how long should the people seek Yahweh?
a: They should seek Yahweh until he comes and blesses them.

q: What did the people trust in for their security rather than in Yahweh?
a: They trusted that their many warriors would protect them.

q: What happened to mothers with their children when Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel?
a: When Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel, mothers were dashed to pieces with their children.

q: Why will the king of Israel be destroyed at Bethel?
a: The king will be destroyed because of the wickedness of the people.

q: From where did Yahweh call Israel when Israel was a young nation?
a: When Israel was a child, Yahweh brought them out of Egypt.

q: What did the Israelites keep doing instead of listening to Yahweh?
a: The Israelites kept offering sacrifices to the Baal gods and burning incense to honor their statues.

q: Who taught Ephraim to walk?
a: Yahweh taught Ephraim to walk.

q: How did Yahweh lead his people?
a: Yahweh gently guided them because he loved them.

q: Who will rule over them since they refuse to worship Yahweh?
a: The king of Assyria will rule over them because they refused to worship Yahweh any more.

q: What will happen to Israel’s cities because of their evil plans?
a: Enemies will attack their cities with swords, destroy the bars of their gates, and kill the people.

q: What are Yahweh’s people determined to do?
a: Yahweh’s people are determined to turn away and stop worshiping him.

q: What happened to the cities of Admah and Zeboiim that Yahweh wants to avoid doing to Ephraim and Israel?
a: Yahweh doesn’t want to destroy Ephraim and Israel the way he destroyed the cities of Admah and Zeboiim because he loves them too much.

q: Why will Yahweh not destroy Ephraim again?
a: Although Yahweh is extremely angry, he will not destroy Ephraim again, for he is God and not a human.

q: What will happen to the people when Yahweh calls out?
a: The Israelites will return to Yahweh and will come back from lands around the sea.

q: What does Yahweh say he will do when the people return?
a: He will settle them in their homes again.

q: Who still follows God?
a: Judah still remains faithful and obeys God.

q: What did Ephraim do to get help from other nations?
a: Ephraim made a treaty with Assyria and sent oil to Egypt.

q: What did Yahweh punish Jacob for?
a: Yahweh punished the descendants of Jacob for how they lived and the things they had done.

q: What did Jacob do in the womb?
a: In the womb, Jacob grabbed his brother by the heel.

q: Where did God speak to Jacob?
a: God spoke with Jacob at Bethel.

q: By what name were the people commanded to call God?
a: The name “Yahweh” is the name that he commanded the people to always use.

q: For what should the people wait?
a: They should wait continually for their God by trusting in him.

q: What do the merchants use to cheat people?
a: The merchants use dishonest scales to cheat people.

q: What did Ephraim claim no one would find in his work?
a: He boasted that in all of his labor, no one will find anything wrong that would be considered sin.

q: Where did the people live when Yahweh brought them out of Egypt?
a: The people lived in tents when they left the land of Egypt.

q: What did Yahweh use the prophets to give to the people?
a: Yahweh used the prophets to give visions and parables to the people.

q: What will Gilgal’s altars be like?
a: Gilgal’s altars will be like piles of stones left on a plowed field.

q: Where did Jacob flee?
a: Jacob fled to the land of Aram to escape from his brother Esau.

q: What did Yahweh do by a prophet?
a: Yahweh used the prophet Moses when he brought Israel up from Egypt, and by that same prophet, he took care of them.

q: What will Ephraim’s Lord do to him?
a: His Lord will hold Ephraim responsible for the bloodshed and give him what he deserves.

q: Why did Ephraim become guilty?
a: He became guilty by worshiping Baal.

q: What do the people have made from their silver?
a: Skilled craftsmen make idols for the people from their silver.

q: What happens to chaff?
a: Chaff is blown away from the threshing floor by the wind.

q: Who does Yahweh say is the only savior for his people?
a: Yahweh says that he himself is the only savior for his people.

q: Where did Yahweh remind the people that he had cared for them?
a: Yahweh cared for his people in the wilderness, in the dry desert land.

q: What happened when the people’s hunger was satisfied?
a: When Yahweh’s people had enough to satisfy their hunger, they became proud and forgot him.

q: What will Yahweh be like to his people?
a: Yahweh will be like a fierce lion, and like a leopard that watches along the path to attack.

q: Like what will Yahweh attack his people?
a: He will attack them like a bear that is robbed of her cubs.

q: Why did Israel’s destruction happen?
a: Israel’s destruction happened because they rebelled against Yahweh, their helper.

q: What did the people ask Yahweh to give them?
a: The people asked Yahweh to give them a king and princes.

q: What did Yahweh do to the king he gave them?
a: Yahweh took the king away because of his wrath.

q: What does Yahweh do with Ephraim’s sin?
a: Yahweh stores up and keeps a record of Ephraim’s sin.

q: What did Yahweh wish he could rescue the people from?
a: Yahweh wanted to save them from death.

q: What will Ephraim’s enemy plunder?
a: His enemy will plunder the treasury of all their valuable objects.

q: What will happen to Samaria’s young children?
a: Their young children will be dashed to pieces.

q: Why should Israel begin to worship and obey Yahweh again?
a: Israel should return to worshiping Yahweh because terrible things are happening to them because of their sin.

q: What does Israel ask Yahweh to do?
a: Israel asks Yahweh to forgive their sin since they now say they will do what is good.

q: Who will not be able to save Israel?
a: Assyria will not save Israel.

q: Why will Yahweh love Israel generously?
a: Yahweh will love them generously because he will no longer be angry with them.

q: What does Yahweh say he will be like to Israel?
a: Yahweh says he will be like the dew that the refreshes the ground to Israel and they will prosper and become strong as the trees of Lebanon.

q: What will Israel’s splendor be like?
a: Israel’s splendor will be as majestic as an olive tree and as delightful as the aroma of the trees in Lebanon.

q: How will the people speak of Yahweh?
a: They will speak well of Yahweh, like they speak well of the fine wine of Lebanon.

q: What does Yahweh say about idols to Ephraim?
a: Yahweh says he wants nothing more to do with idols, and that he is the one who watches over them and is the source of everything good in their lives.

q: Who will walk in the ways of Yahweh?
a: The righteous will walk in Yahweh’s ways and obey him.
